I tested on my macbook pro with : macOS Sequoia (15.7.7) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Dedicated built-in 4GB VRAM AMD Radeon Pro 555X - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-8950HK CPU @ 2.90GHz (12 threads) - 32.00 GiB of 2400Mhz DDR4 memory. The versions that I tested was v4.7.stable.official, v4.8.dev.custom_build (2c089e9bf).
Results : the bug did not occur.
I don't know why it happened on your mac @nmmaroti, maybe because we have different systems,....

I can verify that I am experiencing the same issue on my MacBook Pro and it blocks usage of the Godot editor for me.

My system information is

macOS Ventura (13.7.8) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Intel Iris Plus Graphics 1536 - 2.3 GHz Quad-Core Intel Core i7 processor - 32 GiB memory

I was using the 4.7-stable .NET version.


This may or may not be related - when I launch our project via a run configuration in JetBrains Rider, using that same 4.7-stable .NET version (using the "/Applications/Godot_mono.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot" executable and the "--path MyProjectName" argument), the project hard crashes with perfect repeatability when using that 4.7 version. I may be seeing the same underlying issue, but I can't confirm it's identical.

@samlindsaylevine Your system is:

- macOS Ventura 13.7.8
- Intel Iris Plus Graphics
- Intel Core i7
- Godot 4.7 Stable Mono

Instead of only getting a black editor window, Godot reports VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST and then crashes. Since both issues occur on Intel Macs running Ventura, affect Godot 4.7, and involve the Mobile/Forward+ rendering path while Compatibility works (or is expected to work), they may share the same underlying Vulkan/MoltenVK regression. However, I can't verify that they're the same root cause.

@nmmaroti @samlindsaylevine Can you look into [bisecting the regression](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/feedback/bisecting.html)?

For bisecting, use these commit hashes:

```
git bisect start
git bisect good 89cea1439
git bisect bad bf95b6258
```

I don't have access to an Intel Mac, so this is essential to be able to troubleshoot the issue.

Might be the same issue as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/120973#issuecomment-4889874474. It's upstream MoltenVK issue with low-end Intel Mac GPUs, should be fixed in last [Vulkan SDK release](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/sdk/home#mac), if you can test custom builds, try installing latest Vulkan SDK and rebuilding Godot with it (build system should automatically pick up latest installed SDK).
@nmmaroti are you able to follow this up?

> 12\. [@nmmaroti](https://github.com/nmmaroti) are you able to follow this up? Hey, there! So sorry for the long wait. I didn't get to dissecting the issue, but after [this](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-build-scripts/pull/173) caught my eye I thought to revisit the issue and test some of the 4.8 experimental releases. I'm happy to say I have some good news to share! I tested the following 4.8 experimental releases: v4.8.dev1.official [ebbf577a0] v4.8.dev2.official [7220d456d] v4.8.dev3.official [51105ccbe] v4.8.dev4.official [b56a91878] v4.8.dev5.official [9552dfb68] v4.8.dev6.official [8898c2b3d] v4.8.dev7.official [c971f93e7] Starting from v4.8.dev4.official [b56a91878] and onwards, I can now say that this issue is fully resolved! The the Godot editor now opens without any issues across all three renderers. Cheers!
